t: This is Grosvenor Street, running east from the southeast corner of Grosvenor Square towards Bond Street. It was once called Lower Grosvenor Street, and one early visitor described it as full of excellent houses, mostly lived in by titled and wealthy families. The Alexandra Club, a private members club for women, was here from 1884 until 1939, and the Royal Institute of British Architects was for a time at number sixteen. Frederick William Pavy, the physician who discovered Pavy disease, died here, as did Brigadier-General Richard Ingoldsby. Samuel Henry Faudel-Phillips also lived on the street.
